items.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well do you have any last words for our young jazz people at school, or Mike do you have something?

ctx.x: It’s interesting. I’ve been to Japan a fair amount, and they’re so serious about the music. I guess that’s the Japanese, it’s a very authoritarian, a very patriarchal society. I don’t know whether that explains it or not. But I remember playing, I was over there with a bunch of guys led by Benny Carter, and this was 1985, and we were sitting around like this after a concert, and a guy comes in with a shopping bag. And he doesn’t go to all these other guys who were much better known that I was. But he comes to me…
Well do you have any last words for our young jazz people at school, or Mike do you have something?

Yeah. I wanted to just ask you if you could give a word to young people, college age people, that you know are going to see this interview in years to come. If you could give them just a piece of advice about listening to and participating in or appreciating this music. Any hints? Any insights that would help them get handles on it, quickly and easily?
